statement: The top-8 edit gives a weak dose of RL's policy on every sample, and top8 plain's quick wrong answers are the plain prompt's own failures. Which problems fail is a property of the problem (its difficulty plus prompt-specific traps), not a flat ~50 % coin flip taken per sample whatever the difficulty, so the plain base's errors track how hard the problem is and repeat across independent plain samples of the same problem.
why_strongest: It gives the same three measured values as the theory. The 22 quick wrong answers are short (0.77 at <= 1,000 tokens) because they are plain-register answers. They sit mostly on problems the cued base solves (mean 0.82; 0.25 are cued 4/4) because the plain prompt fails on its own set of problems, and that set is not the cued base's hard set. It also fits the board: the plain base is wrong on 276/500 at T 1.0, self-opened plain answers are 0.21 more accurate at T 0.6, and per-problem propensity dominates same-seed reruns. The theory as its advocate defends it adds one claim: the plain register is wrong at a flat rate whatever the difficulty (about 0.5 at T 1.0, about 0.36 at T 0.6), drawn independently on each sample. That claim makes the quick wrong answers land on cued-easy problems, but it also makes two predictions about the plain base's own stored rows: plain-register accuracy should not depend on the cued base's solve rate, and two independent plain samples of the same problem should fail independently once difficulty is held fixed. The rival says both are false. Any model's errors depend strongly on difficulty and are correlated within a problem. That is the simpler, better-measured mechanism, and the tests below check it directly.

tests.experiment: Difficulty dependence of the plain register at T 1.0. Among plain-base T 1.0 answers that do not self-open, accuracy on problems the cued base solves in all 4 Day-1 #3 samples minus accuracy on problems it solves in at most 1 of 4.
tests.recipe: Files: S3 s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl (base, plain, T 1.0; fetch with the aws command in inventory.md) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. In T3, keep the first row per problem_index in file order. Score it with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from text and gold. An empty extraction counts 0, and a cap_hit row counts 0. Drop T3 rows whose first 60 characters of text contain the substring '\nOkay' (self-opened). In rows.jsonl keep rows with attempt == 0. For each problem_index with exactly 4 such rows, k = the number with score_v3 == 1. Drop problems without exactly 4. Group E = remaining T3 problems with k == 4; group H = remaining T3 problems with k <= 1. Statistic: (mean v3 score of the T3 rows in E) - (mean v3 score of the T3 rows in H). If either group is empty, report nothing.
tests.theory_should_say: The advocate's plain register is wrong about half the time whatever the difficulty, so its accuracy is the same on cued-easy and cued-hard problems, a difference near 0 (within about +-0.15). The rival puts plain-base failures on hard problems, so the gap is about 0.4.

tests.experiment: Difficulty dependence of the plain register at T 0.6. The same contrast on the plain base's T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 answers that do not self-open: accuracy on cued-4/4 problems minus accuracy on cued <= 1/4 problems.
tests.recipe: Files: S3 s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (base, plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95; fetch with the aws command in inventory.md) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. In P_math500, keep for each problem_index the row with the smallest sample value. Score it with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from text and gold. An empty extraction counts 0, and a cap_hit row counts 0. Drop rows whose first 60 characters of text contain '\nOkay' (self-opened). k per problem as in the previous recipe: attempt == 0 rows of rows.jsonl, exactly 4 required, k = count of score_v3 == 1. Group E = kept problems with k == 4; group H = kept problems with k <= 1. Statistic: (mean v3 score over E) - (mean v3 score over H). If either group is empty, report nothing.
tests.theory_should_say: With the plain register at a flat ~0.36 wrong rate whatever the difficulty, accuracy on cued-easy and cued-hard problems would match, a gap near 0. The rival expects a gap of about 0.55.

tests.experiment: Per-problem persistence of plain-base failures at fixed difficulty. On problems the cued base solves in all 4 samples, the plain-base T 1.0 wrong rate when the plain-base T 0.6 answer to the same problem is wrong, minus the T 1.0 wrong rate when that T 0.6 answer is right.
tests.recipe: Files: S3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl (plain, T 1.0), S3 r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (plain, T 0.6; for each problem_index the row with the smallest sample value) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. In T3, keep the first row per problem_index. Score every kept T3 and P_math500 row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py) from text and gold. Wrong = v3 score 0, or cap_hit true, or an empty extraction. No self-open filter is applied. Problem set: problem_index values with exactly 4 attempt-0 rows in rows.jsonl, all 4 with score_v3 == 1, and a kept row in both T3 and P_math500. Within that set, a = (T3-wrong among P-wrong problems) / (P-wrong problems) and b = (T3-wrong among P-right problems) / (P-right problems). Statistic: a - b. If either conditioning group is empty, report nothing.
tests.theory_should_say: Under the advocate's account, plain-register errors are independent per-sample draws that ignore the problem, so on a fixed set of cued-easy problems a T 0.6 failure says nothing about the T 1.0 sample, giving a - b near 0 (about -0.1 to +0.1). The rival's per-problem failures give about 0.22.
